title: Automate the boring report before you analyse it
body:
Every recurring report has a quiet tax: the same copy, paste and check, repeated until someone makes a mistake. I try to pay that tax down before I touch the analysis.

## Start with the repeat offenders

List the steps you did last time. Anything you did twice in the same way is a candidate. In Excel that is often a short VBA macro. In a larger flow it is a scheduled script or an ETL step.

## Keep a check you can read

Automation without a check just makes errors faster. I add a small reconciliation, such as row counts in and out, so a broken run is obvious on the first look.

title: Five SQL habits that save me time
body:
None of these are clever. They just make a query easier to read six weeks later.

## Name the grain

Before writing a join, say in a comment what one row of the result represents. Most wrong totals come from a join that quietly changed the grain.

```
-- one row per placement per week
SELECT placement_id, week_start, SUM(units) AS units
FROM   sales
GROUP  BY placement_id, week_start;
```

Then count rows before and after each join. If the number moves when it should not, you found the problem early.
